This index lists every numbered equation in the volume, by page. It is generated
from the page sources rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot drift out of
step with them.

Equation numbers restart at (1) on each page. They are written inside the
mathematics rather than with the usual tagging command, because MediaWiki's TeX
checker does not accept it; see [[Hamilton's principle/Notation|Notation]].

'''319 numbered equations across 35 pages.'''

Expressions longer than one table cell holds are not reproduced here: 90 of
them are marked and left on their own pages. They are not truncated, because a cut
expression is invalid mathematics and would fail the volume's own checks.

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || Statement || <math>J[y] = \int_a^b L(x, y, y')\, dx</math>
|-
| (2) || Statement || <math>K[y] = \int_a^b M(x, y, y')\, dx = \ell</math>
|-
| (3) || Statement || <math>L^* = L + \mu M</math>
|-
| (4) || Derivation || <math>y_{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2} = y + \varepsilon_1\eta_1 + \varepsilon_2\eta_2</math>
|-
| (5) || Derivation || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (6) || Derivation || <math>\nabla\Phi(0,0) + \mu\,\nabla\Psi(0,0) = 0</math>
|-
| (7) || Derivation || <math>\delta J[y;\eta_j] + \mu\,\delta K[y;\eta_j] = 0, \qquad j = 1, 2</math>
|-
| (8) || Derivation || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (9) || Worked example: the catenary, done properly || <math>J[y] = \int_a^b y\sqrt{1 + y'^2}\; dx</math>
|-
| (10) || Worked example: the catenary, done properly || <math>K[y] = \int_a^b \sqrt{1 + y'^2}\; dx = \ell</math>
|-
| (11) || Worked example: the catenary, done properly || <math>L^* = (y + \mu)\sqrt{1 + y'^2}</math>
|-
| (12) || Worked example: the catenary, done properly || <math>\frac{y + \mu}{\sqrt{1 + y'^2}} = C</math>
|-
| (13) || Worked example: the catenary, done properly || <math>y = -\mu + C\cosh\!\left( \frac{x - x_0}{C} \right)</math>
|-
| (14) || Several constraints || <math>L^* = L + \sum_{\gamma=1}^{s} \mu_\gamma M_\gamma</math>
|-
| (15) || Mixed problems || <math>L^* = L + \sum_\beta \lambda_\beta(x)\, g_\beta + \sum_\gamma \mu_\gamma\, M_\gamma</math>
|}

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-

| (2) || Definition || ''long expression; see the page''

| (3) || Computing it || ''long expression; see the page''

| (4) || Computing it || ''long expression; see the page''

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-

== [[Hamilton's principle/Mathematics/The Weierstrass excess function|the Weierstrass excess function]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || The excess function || <math>E(x, y, p, q) = L(x, y, q) - L(x, y, p) - (q - p)\, L_{y'}(x, y, p)</math>
|-
| (2) || The excess function || <math>E = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - p)^2\, L_{y'y'}(x, y, \bar p)</math>
|-

|-
| (4) || Worked example: where the strong claim fails || <math>J[y] = \int_0^1 \bigl( y'^2 - y'^4 \bigr) dx</math>
|-
| (5) || Worked example: where the strong claim fails || <math>L_{y'y'} = 2 - 12y'^2</math>
|-
| (6) || Worked example: where the strong claim fails || <math>E(x, y, 0, q) = (q^2 - q^4) - 0 - q\cdot 0 = q^2(1 - q^2)</math>
|-
| (7) || Worked example: where the strong claim fails || <math>J[y_n] = \int_0^1 (4 - 16)\, dx = -12</math>
|}

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || The construction || <math>p = f'(v)</math>
|-

|-
| (3) || The geometric reading || <math>h(v) = pv - f(v)</math>

|-

|-
| (8) || Passive variables || <math>\frac{\partial g}{\partial u} = -\frac{\partial f}{\partial u}</math>
|-
| (9) || Passive variables || ''long expression; see the page''

== [[Hamilton's principle/Mathematics/Abbreviated action: Maupertuis versus Hamilton|Abbreviated action: Maupertuis versus Hamilton]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || The two quantities || <math>S = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} L\, dt = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} (T - V)\, dt</math>
|-
| (2) || The two quantities || <math>W = \int \sum_i p_i\, dq_i = \int 2T\, dt</math>
|-
| (3) || The two quantities || <math>W = S + \int H\, dt = S + E\,(t_1 - t_0)</math>
|-
| (4) || Deriving Maupertuis from Hamilton || <math>\delta W = \delta S + E\,\delta(t_1 - t_0)</math>
|-
| (5) || Deriving Maupertuis from Hamilton || <math>\delta W = 0</math>
|-
| (6) || Jacobi's form || <math>W = \int \sqrt{2\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)}\; ds, \qquad ds^2 = \sum_{i,k} g_{ik}\, dq_i\, dq_k</math>
|-
| (7) || Jacobi's form || <math>\tilde g_{ik} = 2\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)\, g_{ik}</math>
|}

== [[Hamilton's principle/Applications/The brachistochrone|the brachistochrone]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || Setting up the functional || <math>\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = mg_0 y \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad v = \sqrt{2g_0 y}</math>
|-
| (2) || Setting up the functional || <math>J[y] = \int_0^{x_1} \frac{\sqrt{1 + y'^2}}{\sqrt{2g_0 y}}\; dx</math>
|-
| (3) || Solving || <math>L = \sqrt{\frac{1 + y'^2}{y}}</math>
|-
| (4) || Solving || <math>L - y'\,\frac{\partial L}{\partial y'} = C_1</math>
|-
| (5) || Solving || <math>\frac{\partial L}{\partial y'} = \frac{y'}{\sqrt{y}\,\sqrt{1 + y'^2}}</math>
|-
| (6) || Solving || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (7) || Solving || <math>y\,(1 + y'^2) = k^2, \qquad k^2 = 1/C_1^2</math>
|-
| (8) || Integrating || <math>y' = \sqrt{\frac{k^2 - y}{y}}</math>
|-
| (9) || Integrating || <math>dx = \sqrt{\frac{y}{k^2 - y}}\; dy</math>
|-
| (10) || Integrating || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (11) || Integrating || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (12) || Integrating || <math>x = a\,(\theta - \sin\theta), \qquad y = a\,(1 - \cos\theta)</math>
|-
| (13) || Fixing the constants || <math>\frac{x_1}{y_1} = \frac{\theta_1 - \sin\theta_1}{1 - \cos\theta_1}</math>
|-
| (14) || The descent time || <math>t = \sqrt{\frac{a}{g_0}}\; \theta_1</math>
|}

== [[Hamilton's principle/Applications/The catenary|the catenary]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || The functional and the constraint || <math>J[y] = \rho g_0 \int_{x_0}^{x_1} y\,\sqrt{1 + y'^2}\; dx</math>
|-
| (2) || The functional and the constraint || <math>K[y] = \int_{x_0}^{x_1} \sqrt{1 + y'^2}\; dx = \ell</math>
|-
| (3) || The functional and the constraint || <math>L^* = (y + \mu)\sqrt{1 + y'^2}</math>
|-
| (4) || The shape || <math>\frac{y + \mu}{\sqrt{1 + y'^2}} = C</math>
|-
| (5) || The shape || <math>\frac{dy}{\sqrt{(y+\mu)^2/C^2 - 1}} = dx</math>
|-
| (6) || The shape || <math>y = -\mu + C \cosh\!\left( \frac{x - x_0'}{C} \right)</math>
|-
| (7) || Fixing the three constants || ''long expression; see the page''
|-
| (8) || Fixing the three constants || <math>\ell = 2C\sinh\!\left( \frac{d}{C} \right)</math>
|-
| (9) || Reading the multiplier || <math>T_x = \rho g_0 C</math>
|-
| (10) || Reading the multiplier || <math>T = \rho g_0 (y + \mu)</math>
|-
| (11) || The related surface || <math>A = 2\pi\int y\sqrt{1+y'^2}\; dx</math>
|}

== [[Hamilton's principle/Applications/Fermat's principle|Fermat's principle]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || Statement || <math>T = \int \frac{ds}{v} = \frac{1}{c}\int n(x,y,z)\; ds</math>
|-
| (2) || Snell's law || <math>cT(x) = n_1\sqrt{a^2 + x^2} + n_2\sqrt{b^2 + (d-x)^2}</math>
|-
| (3) || Snell's law || <math>c\,\frac{dT}{dx} = \frac{n_1 x}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}} - \frac{n_2 (d-x)}{\sqrt{b^2+(d-x)^2}}</math>
|-
| (4) || Snell's law || <math>n_1 \sin\theta_1 = n_2 \sin\theta_2</math>
|-
| (5) || The continuous case || <math>J[y] = \int n(x,y)\,\sqrt{1 + y'^2}\; dx</math>
|-
| (6) || The continuous case || <math>\frac{n(y)}{\sqrt{1+y'^2}} = \text{const}</math>
|-
| (7) || Rays are geodesics || <math>d\tilde s^2 = n^2(q)\,\bigl( dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 \bigr)</math>
|-
| (8) || Rays are geodesics || <math>n(q) \;\longleftrightarrow\; \sqrt{2\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)}</math>
|}

== [[Hamilton's principle/Applications/The optical-mechanical analogy|the optical-mechanical analogy]] ==

{| class="wikitable"
! no. !! section !! expression
|-
| (1) || The correspondence || <math>\int n(q)\; ds</math>
|-
| (2) || The correspondence || <math>\int \sqrt{2m\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)}\; ds</math>
|-
| (3) || The correspondence || <math>n(q) \;\longleftrightarrow\; \sqrt{2m\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)}</math>
|-
| (4) || Both are Hamilton-Jacobi || <math>\vert \nabla\Psi \vert^2 = n^2(q), \qquad \vert \nabla W \vert^2 = 2m\bigl(E - V(q)\bigr)</math>
|-
| (5) || Filling the hole || <math>\psi = A(q)\, \exp\!\left( \frac{i\,W(q)}{\hbar} \right)</math>
|-
| (6) || Filling the hole || <math>\vert \nabla W \vert^2 - \hbar^2\,\frac{\nabla^2 A}{A} = \hbar^2 k^2</math>
|-
| (7) || Filling the hole || <math>-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2\psi + V\psi = E\psi</math>
|}
